ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Screening against the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, and SEPBLAC advisories is mandatory before and at notarization; politically exposed persons (PEPs), including shareholders, directors and UBOs, trigger enhanced due diligence under Article 15 Ley 10/2010, with senior-management approval and source-of-funds verification. Despite the low-risk classification, the notary and the opening bank must identify all subscribers and file the UBO declaration in the Registro de Titularidades Reales within prescribed deadlines.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central (Central Commercial Registry; www.rmc.es), processing through certified Notary or CIRCE/PAE electronic channels
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be expressed in alphabetic characters of a language of any State using the Latin alphabet; the certification request is filed in Spanish. Foreign words may be admitted where they are not confusing and are transliterated if required for pronunciation. The SL must end with 'Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada' or 'S.L.', and the denomination must be truthful, distinctive, and not identical or confusingly similar to any pre-existing registered name.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Words implying official or royal sponsorship: 'España', 'Spanish', 'Estado', 'Gobierno', 'Corona', 'Real', 'Banco de España' (require ministerial or Council of Ministers authorization)
Geographic-scope qualifiers denoting cross-border or mass operations: 'Internacional', 'Mundial', 'Europeo', 'Iberoamericano' (denied unless actual foreign activity is evidenced)
Names of other states, sub-state territories, international organizations, or protected insignia such as 'ONU', 'UE', 'OTAN', 'Cruz Roja'
Misleading references to business activities not actually to be carried out
Terms contrary to Spanish law, public order, or buen costumbre, and denominations conflicting with earlier registered trademarks
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a negative name certificate, the applicant may (i) file a new application with alternative candidate names via the same RMC electronic channel, or (ii) within one month of notification submit a written administrative recourse (recurso de alzada) to the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública (DGSJFP) under Ley 39/2015, adducing evidence of prior entitlement or absence of identity; the RMC may also grant one renewal of the existing certificate for a further 90 days if requested before expiry. Contencioso-administrativo court review is available after exhaustion of administrative remedies.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditionally permissible for a non-licensed PR agency: the registered office must be a genuine address in Spanish territory capable of receiving notifications and official correspondence. A serviced office, co-working space or business-center address with a valid tenancy or address-management contract is accepted by notaries and the Registro Mercantil; a mere post-office box is not acceptable. AEAT and bank AML checks will insist on documentary proof of the address arrangement.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (approximately 5% within the first 24 months) because the activity is non-regulated and low-risk; nevertheless, AEAT retains unannounced on-site verification powers under Ley 58/2003 General Tributaria and the Registro Mercantil may send follow-up postal verifications of the registered office.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) – Sede Electrónica (sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident entity must appoint a tax representative resident in Spain and file Form 030 (or 036 as appropriate) with AEAT to obtain a foreign entity's NIF (Número de Identificación Fiscal). Supporting notarized and apostilled incorporation documents, a certificate of residence from the home tax authority, and evidence of the Spanish nexus (e.g., PE or invoicing activity) are required. Registration is effected before the local tax office or electronically with a recognized e-certificate. The NIF must be quoted on all invoices, customs declarations and tax returns.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box entity classification election under Spanish domestic law; an SL is automatically a taxable person for Corporate Income Tax. Hybrid mismatch adjustments follow EU ATAD (Directive 2016/1164) and domestic Law 27/2014, which may re-characterise payments involving transparent entities. Optional regimes requiring an election include SOCIMI (Real Estate Investment Company) and ETVE (foreign-securities holding company), both subject to strict qualifying conditions.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (IVA – Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general turnover threshold; registration is obligatory from the first taxable transaction carried out in Spanish territory. A special EUR 10,000 intra-EU threshold applies to distance sales of goods and cross-border digital services under the OSS non-union scheme.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Ley Crea y Crece (Law 18/2022) mandates electronic invoicing in B2B transactions, to be phased in under implementing regulations. Large enterprises and businesses subject to the Suministro Inmediato de Información (SII) regime must submit VAT transaction records to AEAT through web services (API/SOAP-REST) within four days (eight for certain taxpayers). Verifactu-certified invoicing software with QR/encryption integrity requirements is compulsory for all entities issuing invoices, though no fiscal stamp or real-time clearance approval is applied; SII effectively provides near real-time fiscal clearing.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods dispatched or transported to a non-EU destination are subject to export exemption (0% VAT) under Art. 21 LIVA, provided the exporter retains proof of physical departure. Services to non-EU customers are generally not taxable in Spain under the place-of-supply rule; input VAT on costs directly attributable to such operations is recoverable when supported by adequate documentation. Certain services listed in Art. 21 LIVA (e.g., brokering or commission services for exports, freight, storage ancillary to export) are expressly exempt with credit.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DUA – Single Administrative Document)
Bill of Lading, CMR or Airway Bill evidencing dispatch from Spanish / EU territory
Bank Inward Remittance Certificate (SWIFT MT103 or bank confirmation of payment received)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Unsubstantiated or fictitious zero-rated exports trigger regularisation by AEAT, reversal of input VAT deductions, late payment interest, and tax penalties ranging from 50% to 150% of the tax amount involved under Articles 191 and 193 of the General Tax Law. If the 180-day FX repatriation deadline (extendable under specific rules) is not met without justification, export exemption is clawed back. Fraudulent conduct involving VAT amounts exceeding EUR 120,000 may constitute a criminal offence under the Spanish Criminal Code, carrying prison sentences and corporate liability.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), acting in coordination with the Ministry of Economy and Digital Transformation and the Comisión Nacional del Mercado de Valores (CNMV) for matters involving securities and investment services.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain, as a Eurozone member, maintains full convertibility for both current account transactions (goods, services, royalties, dividends, retained earnings) and capital account transactions (foreign direct investment, portfolio investment, financial loans) under the free movement of capital enshrined in Articles 63–66 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union. No prior foreign exchange authorization is required for profit repatriation or import/export settlements. Residual procedural hurdles arise exclusively from statistical reporting obligations, anti-money-laundering (AML) compliance, and, where applicable, withholding tax on outbound dividends (generally 19% absent a treaty or an EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive exemption), which is a tax measure, not a currency or convertibility restriction.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Spain imposes no mandatory surrender or repatriation requirement on export proceeds. The exporting entity may retain foreign currency in compliant foreign currency accounts at domestic or EU-authorised banks, may freely transfer the proceeds to non-resident beneficiaries for settlement of trade payables, or may convert to EUR at market rates. However, transactions above the threshold of EUR 100,000 (or equivalent) must be declared to Banco de España for balance-of-payments statistical purposes on the standard CBE (Comunicación de Balanza de Pagos) forms. Failure to submit timely declarations within the statutory reporting window may result in administrative fines under Law 10/2010 and related regulations.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility. Authorised EU electronic money institutions (EMIs) such as Revolut Business, N26 Business, and Bnext (Spain) may be used for low-risk treasury operations: EUR SEPA transfers, expense card issuance, and multi-currency wallets. They offer rapid remote onboarding and often enable receiving USD, MXN, and BRL payments through corresponding banking arrangements. However, EMIs are not credit institutions and may not provide commercial credit, documentary credits, or complex FX derivatives. Legal constraints under the E-Money Directive (Directive 2009/110/EC) require safeguarding of client funds at designated banks, and the PR firm's principal operational account for statutory capital traceability, tax authority compliance, and material trade settlements should remain with a tier-1 credit institution.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is generally expected at tier-1 banks for non-resident corporate clients, particularly for the director(s) and the ultimate beneficial owner(s) (UBO). Some progressive banks, including fintech-oriented entities and certain Madrid-based branches of international banks, accept remote identity verification via qualified electronic signatures and video-identification under the Anti-Money-Laundering Act 10/2010 and the European AML Directives, provided the client obtains a NIE (Número de Identificación de Extranjero) and completes a notarised corporate approval resolution. For conservative institutions, the directors of the Spanish SL must attend a face-to-face interview at the branch or grant a Spain-resident attorney a notarial power of attorney (Poder General) to perform the KYC interview on their behalf; failure to establish physical substance can lead to rejection.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial capital contribution from a non-resident shareholder with insufficient proof of legitimate source of funds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised capital subscription agreement, audited or bank-certified shareholder financial statements for the prior two years, six months of bank statements showing the transaction trail, a source-of-wealth declaration signed by the UBO, and evidence of the shareholder's tax registration (e.g., UK Corporation Tax or US EIN equivalent).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained recurring retainer inflows from a small number of overseas PR clients in high-risk jurisdictions (e.g., Panama, BVI, UAE).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed retainer contracts with defined deliverables, factual timesheets and campaign reports, compliant commercial invoices aligned with the transfer amount, correspondent bank details of the payee, client beneficial ownership documentation, and proof of the SL's internal AML risk assessment and client diligence procedure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Outbound payments to related overseas group companies for delegated services, potentially perceived as profit stripping or unauthorised financial flows.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Transfer pricing report or comparability study demonstrating arm's length remuneration, intercompany service agreements, evidence of contractual milestones and operational business purpose, tax residency certificates of the counterparties, and Spanish corporate tax filings (Form 200) confirming reporting of the transactions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inability to verify the identity, residential address, and professional reputation of directors and UBOs without previous EU banking history.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid passports and identity cards, NIE or Spanish tax ID certificate, utility bills and notarised proof of address, criminal record certificate issued by the home country, regulatory or professional references from senior professionals, and a notarised corporate resolution approving the opening of the account together with a list of authorised signatories.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital contributions to the Spanish SL must be executed by SWIFT MT103 wire transfer from the foreign shareholder's bank to the SL's capital escrow account. The transfer must include the shareholder's bank reference and a precise purpose code that matches the foreign direct investment nature, typically the Spanish balance-of-payments entry for direct equity investments (code F/I or the bank's equivalent). Following receipt, the SL must record the contribution and file the corresponding foreign investment declaration with the Register of Foreign Investments within one month after notarisation of the deed of capital increase. The bank will require the final executed deed, the certificate of the notary, and the Corporate Tax (Form) to be presented before the funds are released to the operational account. Verification of the beneficial ownership of the incoming wire is mandatory pursuant to Law 10/2010.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For outbound trade settlements, the SL should utilise SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) for all EUR-denominated payments to EU beneficiaries, with immediate clearing by plain-vanilla bank credit rails. For non-EU, non-EUR payments (for example fees to Latin American partner agencies or production houses), the mandatory rail is SWIFT MT103 with correspondent banking, executed via the SL's tier-1 Spanish bank using the beneficiary's IBAN/account number and intermediary bank codes. Commercial Letters of Credit (Documentary or Standby LCs) are permissible for long-term retainer or event-production contracts involving substantial prepayments, enabling documentary compliance through banks rather than direct cash remittances. All outgoing transfers must identify the statutory purpose code for balance-of-payments reporting, and any transfer exceeding EUR 100,000 triggers automatic CBE reporting duties.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Foreign exchange forward contracts (deliverable FX forwards against EUR/USD, EUR/MXN, and EUR/COP) executed under a negotiated ISDA or short-form derivatives agreement, aligned with forecast retainer inflows and dividend repatriation timelines.
Foreign exchange swaps (FX swaps, tom/next and spot/forward structures) for efficient intra-period liquidity clearing and rollover of short term currency exposures.

Cross-currency basis swaps (EUR against USD or MXN) used to hedge long-term net investments in Latin American subsidiaries or loan participation assets, subject to IFRS hedge accounting documentation.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) specifically for currencies with restricted convertibility or thin offshore deliverable markets (e.g., Argentine peso, Venezuelan equivalent securities) with EUR or USD settlement, anchored by a cash-flow exposure model and underlying PR service contracts.

European-style currency options (call and put combinations, zero-cost collars and exotic barrier structures approved by compliance) to protect the P&L against unfavourable rate movements while enabling participation in favourable trends; all OTC derivative trades must comply with EMIR clearing, margin, and trade reporting requirements.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of Annual Accounts (Cuentas Anuales) in the Mercantile Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one (1) month from the shareholders' approval meeting; the meeting must be held within six (6) months after the corporate fiscal year-end (e.g., by 31 July for a 31 December year-end).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers closure of the company's registration sheet (cierre registral) after 18 months, preventing further valid filings; administrative fines under Ley de Sociedades de Capital art. 283 range from EUR 1,200 to EUR 60,000 depending on egregiousness.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Impuesto sobre Sociedades, Modelo 200)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 25 calendar days following the six (6) months after the tax year-end (e.g., by 25 July for a 31 December year-end).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing incurs a 5% to 20% surcharge plus late-payment interest (current annual rate around 3.75%); penalties for false or understated returns are 15% to 50% of the shortfall.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Economic Activities Tax (IAE) Annual Declaration / Exemption filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually from 1 February to 15 February for updated IAE census data or new activity triggering the filing; companies with annual turnover above EUR 1,000,000 must submit Modelo 848 / IAE statement.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or filing untimely incurs a penalty for breach of tax residence information duties: EUR 1,500 to EUR 10,000 per year or 50% of the tax base omitted.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) Register Update Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Mercantil / SEPBLAC legal framework (Registro de Titularidades Reales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No fixed annual national filing; updates must be recorded and reflected in the internal UBO ledger immediately upon any ownership change or beneficial ownership transfer, with corresponding notarial registration at the time of share transfer.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance with UBO register maintenance or false statements is an infringement under the Spanish anti-money-laundering law, subject to fines ranging from EUR 60,000 to EUR 2,000,000 for serious offenses and potential rejection of corporate filings.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit for a Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada if, for two (2) consecutive fiscal years, the company exceeds at least two (2) of the following: total assets > EUR 4,000,000; net annual turnover > EUR 8,000,000; average headcount > 50 employees. Other triggers: regulated financial entities, multi-parent groups, or high litigation risk.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (PGC - Plan General Contable) in accordance with EU Accounting Directive 2013/34/EU; IFRS required for consolidated group accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Spanish law, every SL must maintain an internal 'Registro de Titularidades Reales' (UBO ledger). Although Spain does not levy a separate national annual UBO filing, any share transfer must be notarized and registered with the Mercantile Registry; the UBO ledger must be simultaneously updated and made available to National Securities Market Commission / tax authorities when requested.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Inventory and Annual Accounts Book (Libro de Inventarios y Cuentas Anuales)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: EUR 300–EUR 800 per year (≈ USD 320–850), depending on provincial commercial registry and legal agent services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: EUR 1,800–EUR 4,500 (≈ USD 1,900–4,800) for a small non-audit-exempt SL based on transaction volume and balance-sheet complexity; lower if only review procedures are performed

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 25% headline rate; R&D tax credit up to 100% of eligible expenses; accelerated depreciation; no general tax holidays applicable to PR services
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited with 25% annual limitation on deductible losses

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 100 - Annual Corporate Income Tax Return; filed electronically through Agencia Tributaria e-Spain portal (Cl@ve, digital certificate or equivalent)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 25 days after the end of the tax period (e.g., 25 April for calendar year ending 31 December)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable base before incentives and losses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Adjust for any permanent establishment attribution if services rendered abroad
Limited applicability for non-residents without PE

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: 100% to 200% of the tax due plus daily surcharge of 20-60 EUR per day; criminal sanctions possible for willful non-filing

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% on gross dividends distributed to non-resident shareholders (treaty reduction to 5-15% possible)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Obtain Spanish Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from AEAT; submit Form 210 (or equivalent) to withholding agent with TRC and beneficial ownership declaration
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 19% standard rate, reduced under most treaties (e.g. 0-10%); Interest on debt: 19% standard, often reduced to 0% under OECD-compliant treaties

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 10,000,000 (group consolidated revenue for local file; Master File at EUR 50,000,000)
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Economic Substance Regulations apply to certain qualifying activities (e.g. pure equity holding, IP holding); PR agency generally does not trigger ESR unless structured as such

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of taxable income or failure to declare cross-border transactions
